description.la: De tribus diebus, quem Migne librum septimum Didascalici nominat: visibilia mundi opera tribus attributis divinae Trinitatis (potentia, sapientia, benignitas) illustrantur.
description.en-US: The treatise that Migne prints as the seventh book of the Didascalicon: the visible world as a book written by the finger of God, read as a mirror of the Trinity’s power, wisdom and goodness. Latin only, from the Migne text (Patrologia Latina 176, 1854), a machine-corrected OCR.
description.pt-BR: O tratado que Migne imprime como sétimo livro do Didascálicon: o mundo visível como livro escrito pelo dedo de Deus, lido como espelho do poder, da sabedoria e da bondade da Trindade.

sources.edition: Migne, Patrologia Latina 176 (Paris 1854); TEI XML of the Corpus Corporum (University of Zurich), text HuDeSVi.EruDid, from the machine-corrected OCR of the Open Greek and Latin project.
sources.description: The complete PL text with its chapter divisions. PL page breaks and column numbers are dropped, and the PL tables of chapters (which repeat the chapter headings) are not imported. The OCR carries a few residual slips.
sources.tierEvidence: Migne’s Patrologia Latina (1854–1855) prints the medieval text; public domain everywhere.
